subject: Billing cadence & PO handling for Dedicated GPU pool — invoice split / Net terms / true-up
messages:
From: Lindsay Park <lindsay.park@fintechco.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@fintechco.com; marcus.lee@fintechco.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity billing — invoice cadence / PO question

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday. The team is aligned on the GPU pool sizing you proposed for our production traffic, but our finance team needs clarity on how Redwood will invoice the committed capacity. Two specific asks:

1) Can Redwood split an annual committed-price agreement into 12 monthly invoices (we prefer this for cashflow reconciliation) while still treating it as an annual prepay for contract terms and discounts?

2) We typically issue a PO up front and require Net 45. Are you able to accept a PO + Net 45 for an annual commitment, or do you require Net 30 for discounted pricing?

Also, we wanted to confirm the timing and mechanics of the true-up if our usage exceeds the committed throughput. Would that be charged monthly, quarterly, or only at renewal?

I've attached a draft PO to show our internal format. Can you and your team confirm what you need to proceed?

Appreciate any examples of invoice layouts or sample contract language we can share with Procurement.

Best,
Lindsay
Lindsay Park
Head of Product — FintechCo

Attachments: FintechCo_PO_draft.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lindsay Park <lindsay.park@fintechco.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity billing — invoice cadence / PO question

Hi Lindsay — thanks for the clear note and the PO template. Quick answers up front: yes, we can support a 12-invoice split tied to an annual commitment, and we can accept a customer PO. Net terms and discount level are negotiable (details below).

Options we typically offer for Dedicated (GPU pool) billing:

- Annual prepay (recommended for lowest unit price): full invoice up front, standard 10% prepay discount, billed Net 30. We can, by contract, split the invoice into 12 equal invoices for your AP system while treating it as prepaid for contract purposes (we record the full payment obligation up front).

- Annual prepay with PO + split invoices: we can accept a PO and issue 12 invoices referencing that PO (invoice schedule attached). For finance, Redwood will include an EOM reference and PO number on every invoice. To extend Net 45 instead of our standard Net 30 for this arrangement we would need an approval from finance; see concession path below.

- Monthly reserved commit: billed monthly, no prepay discount. Monthly true-ups are automatic; this gives you more operational flexibility but at a higher unit cost.

True-up mechanics (recommended defaults):
- If you elect annual prepay, usage beyond committed throughput is billed monthly at the overage rate and reflected on the next invoice; a final contractual reconciliation (true-up) occurs at renewal to adjust committed units.
- If you elect monthly reserved commit, overage is billed on the following month’s invoice and we do a quarterly checkpoint for long-term capacity adjustments.

Concession path we can propose to Procurement:
- If FintechCo signs an annual prepay and provides a PO within 14 days of countersignature, Redwood will: 1) accept split invoices (12), and 2) extend Net 45 for the first year only. In return, we ask that the PO reference the attached SOW and that the annual invoiced amount be committed against the PO.

I attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf (pricing options) and a draft invoice schedule (invoice_schedule_split_12.xlsx). Also attaching a redline SOW for the PO wording we recommend (SOW_Redline_2026-07-22.docx).

Please review and let me know which of the billing options your procurement prefers and whether you want me to escalate the Net 45 concession to finance for written approval.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior AM, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf; invoice_schedule_split_12.xlsx; SOW_Redline_2026-07-22.docx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity billing — invoice cadence / PO question

Hannah — copying in pricing ops. My take: offer a middle ground to close quickly. Proposed negotiation bullets to include in your reply to FintechCo:

1) Standard annual prepay: 10% discount, Net 30.
2) Annual prepay + PO + split 12 invoices: accept, but reduce discount to 7% if customer requires Net 45 (finance concession).
3) If customer wants to avoid prepay entirely (monthly reserved commit) then no discount, Net 30, monthly invoices and monthly true-ups.

Also recommend we add explicit language in the SOW: "True-ups will be invoiced monthly for any overage, with a contractual reconciliation at annual renewal. In the event of sustained overages (>25% of committed capacity for two consecutive quarters) Redwood reserves the right to propose an immediate commit increase to preserve SLAs."

If you want, I can provide a one-paragraph concession approval to attach to the quote (authorizing finance to permit Net 45 for year one at 7% discount). For larger discounts we'd need Legal and VP signoff.

Rishi
VP Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@fintechco.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>; rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@fintechco.com; lindsay.park@fintechco.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity billing — invoice cadence / PO question

Hi Hannah & Rishi,

Thanks for the clear options. A couple follow-ups from our FinOps team: we can provide a PO upfront but our policy requires Net 45 across the board for multi-year licensing. Two requests to confirm feasibility:

1) If Redwood will accept Net 45, can you confirm whether the discount stays at 10% or drops to 7% as Rishi suggested? We prefer the full 10% but can agree to 7% if that is the concession for Net 45.

2) For internal controls, we need the invoices split across 12 months (so accounting can amortize on our books) and each invoice must reference the PO. Will Redwood list the full annual SOW and include a line in each invoice that references the unused prepayment balance?

Lastly, on true-ups: we would prefer overages to be billed monthly and credited against the PO balance (rather than additional invoicing) where possible — does Redwood support applying overage dollars to the prepayment balance so we don't have separate remittance flows?

I've attached a lightly annotated PO to show the exact fields our AP system needs.

Thanks,
Marcus Lee
Head of FinOps — FintechCo

Attachments: FintechCo_PO_draft.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@fintechco.com>; Lindsay Park <lindsay.park@fintechco.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity billing — invoice cadence / PO question

Marcus / Lindsay — appreciate the details and the annotated PO. We discussed with Finance and here is the position we can commit to in writing for the first year to help you get this across the finish line:

- Agreement: Redwood will accept FintechCo’s PO and will issue 12 monthly invoices tied to that PO. Each invoice will include: PO number, annual SOW reference, line showing the billed portion of the prepay, and a running prepay balance.

- Net terms: Redwood will accept Net 45 for Year 1 on the annual prepay if the PO is received within 14 days of countersignature. To make this work for us, the effective discount will be 7% (concession approved by Sales leadership). We will document this in a short pricing concession addendum attached to the SOW.

- Overage / true-up handling: Overages will be billed monthly. For Year 1 we will apply overage charges as a credit/debit against the prepay balance on the next scheduled invoice (so no separate remittance flow). At renewal we will perform a contractual reconciliation and adjust the committed units and pricing as appropriate.

- Escalation / SLA preservation: If sustained overages exceed 25% of committed capacity for two consecutive quarters, Redwood may propose a mid-term capacity amendment to preserve SLAs.

Next steps: I attached a redline SOW that inserts the concession language and the invoice layout (SOW_Redline_2026-07-22.docx). If this looks good, please confirm and route the PO to billing@redwood.ai and we will generate the 12 invoices tied to that PO. We will also attach the concession addendum to the executed SOW.

If you need the full 10% discount, we can discuss a different payment arrangement (full upfront prepay Net 30; Finance will re-evaluate).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if you prefer to finalize details.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior AM, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_Redline_2026-07-22.docx; invoice_schedule_split_12.xlsx
